segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show. AppLovin sold its own apps business in June 2025; its results sit in discontinued operations, below.

sources.label: Q2 2025 release — restated continuing-operations statements (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Advertising revenue rose 75% from a year ago to $711M in the quarter — up from $406M in Q2 2023 — as AXON, AppLovin's AI ad engine, kept finding better matches between advertisers and the users inside other companies' apps.
takeaways.title: The platform kept compounding

takeaways.text: The continuing platform turned $711M of revenue into $384M of operating income. Its total costs were just $327M — they barely grow with sales, so most of each new revenue dollar drops through to profit.
takeaways.title: Margins most companies can't match

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $446M in a single quarter — operating cash flow of $455M with only a small amount spent on equipment and finance leases — as the company's profit converted almost dollar-for-dollar into cash.
takeaways.title: Cash poured in

verdict: AppLovin's advertising platform grew revenue 75% from a year ago to $711M and turned it into $301M of profit from continuing operations — a 54% operating margin — while the apps business it later sold chipped in a $9M profit of its own.
